Relative fit depends on guest promise, design intensity, operating complexity, and platform participation—not on parent-company familiarity alone.

before.title: Scaled Select-Service New-Build
before.body: A new-build site where owners want a proven upper-midscale brand with breakfast-led guest expectations and IHG distribution. Holiday Inn Express fits when the market supports consistent midscale demand and the owner can execute the current prototype efficiently. Owner value is strongest when the asset can deliver broad demand base under the Holiday Inn Express promise without stretching capital or operating capacity beyond what the market can support. Weaker when conversion PIP or prototype scope would outrun underwriting.

before.title: Why Value Is Strongest
before.body:
Value for Holiday Inn Express is strongest when the asset can deliver the brand’s specific guest promise and the owner can execute platform obligations with discipline.
- Strongest where new-build and conversion hotels in business, airport, suburban, and selected urban corridors with reliable midscale demand.
- Owner diligence should center on broad demand base, conversion and new-build suitability, efficient operating model, and IHG distribution strength.
- Distinguish from Holiday Inn, avid hotels, EVEN Hotels before selecting this path.
- Weaker where the asset cannot support the Holiday Inn Express guest promise or platform obligations.

after.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
after.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add IHG One Rewards: retain Holiday Inn Express's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Midscale limited-service: efficient rooms, Express Start breakfast, and IHG One Rewards distribution for value-conscious transient demand.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.
